title: Four ways to begin Beethoven’s Fifth
work: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67 — first movement
question: Why do the same four notes sound so different from one conductor to another?
intro: In November 1913, Arthur Nikisch brought the Berlin Philharmonic into the studio to play Beethoven’s Fifth into a recording horn. Odeon’s house orchestra had got there two years earlier. Mengelberg’s Concertgebouw and the Skidmore College Orchestra join them here at the first three Gs. Each conductor must decide how long the fourth note hangs in the air.

recordings.label: Odeon Orchestra, 1911
recordings.note: Odeon’s house orchestra made the first complete recording of a symphony: Beethoven’s Fifth, in Berlin in August 1911.

recordings.label: Arthur Nikisch, 1913
recordings.note: Nikisch takes an unusually broad first movement with the Berlin Philharmonic, leaving out the exposition repeat.

recordings.label: Willem Mengelberg
recordings.note: This opening side catches Mengelberg with the Concertgebouw Orchestra he had led since 1895.

recordings.label: Skidmore College Orchestra
recordings.note: Skidmore takes the exposition repeat, so the horns’ call and the soft E♭-major violin tune have a second hearing.

passages.label: Opening motto, repeated
passages.note: Three Gs fall to E♭; three Fs answer with a held D. Beethoven’s fermatas leave the conductor in charge of the silence.

passages.label: The strings climb
passages.note: The strings climb, passing the short rhythm from part to part. Woodwinds and horns answer before the orchestra swells.

passages.label: The horns open a door
passages.note: A clipped chord and a pause clear the way for the horns. Their wide call opens onto the violins’ soft E♭-major tune.

passages.label: Development
passages.note: Horns call down to G; the strings strike D♭ against it. The familiar rhythm has brought Beethoven into a new argument.

passages.label: The ending starts again
passages.note: High C hangs in the violins while the bass changes beneath it. The expected ending has become the start of a long coda.
